messages.content: Calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test with a sample mean of 98.2, standard deviation of 1.4, and sample size of 40 for a population mean of 98.6.

function.name: statistics_calculate_p_value
function.description: Calculate the p-value for a t-test on a single sample from a population. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

sample_mean.description: The mean of the sample data. This is a float type value.

population_mean.description: The mean of the population data. This is a float type value.

sample_std_dev.description: The standard deviation of the sample data. This is a float type value.

sample_size.description: The size of the sample data.

two_tailed.description: Whether the test is two-tailed. If not provided, default is true.

message.content:
The standard error (i.e., the standard deviation of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under the null hypothesis) is  

\[
SE = \frac{s}{\sqrt{n}} = \frac{1.4}{\sqrt{40}} \approx 0.221.
\]
message.reasoning: We need to calculate the standard deviation of the null hypothesis test? Probably they want the standard error of the mean under null? Standard error = sample_std_dev / sqrt(sample_size). But they mention "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test" maybe they want the standard error of the sampling distribution of the sample mean under null. That is SE = sigma / sqrt(n). So compute 1.4 / sqrt(40). sqrt(40) ≈ 6.3249. 1.4 / 6.3249 ≈ 0.2213. So answer ~0.221. Alternatively, if they want the standard deviation of the test statistic? For t-test, t = (sample_mean - population_mean) / (sample_std_dev / sqrt(n)). The denominator is standard error. So standard deviation of test statistic under null is 1? Actually t distribution has df=39. But they ask "standard deviation of the null hypothesis test". Might be standard error. So answer ~0.221. Let's provide that.
